_about: 30 Shop All concepts from three writers (data-led, platform-native, catalogue and offer), then the editor's 20 and the cut 10.
campaign_idea: Campaign name: NEVER JUST ONE. Every ad starts from a familiar Indian thing that never comes alone: a choodi stack, a masala dabba, Mummy, Didi and me, a haveli wall of windows, three stripes of rangoli, teen patti's three cards, a list of who gets what. That thing opens all 130+ pieces from ₹599, each shown big, named and priced exactly. The multi-buy then lands as the thing's own punchline ('three in a row', 'All of the above. Correct.', '= 20% off', 'That's three'), applied in her bag. It is never a code and never the headline. Four single-winner doors (Almost edible, Rangoli, the Nocturne saree, the anaar necklace) carry the account's proven stops, and the grids, lists, chats and games carry the breadth. The buyer throughout is a woman shopping for herself and the women around her, with no deadline anywhere. Global build rules: ₹ only in CG, CGI, Inter, Kalam, Caveat or Anton, because Jost, Velista, Old Standard and Permanent Marker have no ₹ glyph (several source concepts would have rendered broken prices). Story text and logo sit between y=270 and y=1500. One NAIRA logo per frame, 220-320 px wide.

drafts.why: This ports the batch's top-scoring competitor ad (GIVA gifting list, 6.6) into an object Naira may use (a notebook page, not a receipt), in handwriting, and for her women rather than 'Wife'.
